name: Kuwait
summary: Green, white and red horizontal bands with a black trapezoid at the hoist, in the Pan-Arab colours. It was adopted soon after independence from Britain in 1961, replacing a red flag with the name 'Kuwait'.
origin: Kuwait used red flags, at times with the name of the country or a crescent, until independence in June 1961.
The current flag was officially raised on 24 November 1961. The colours follow the Arab Revolt flag and Pan-Arab tradition, and are described in a line of poetry by Safi al-Din al-Hilli.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the enemy on Kuwaiti swords.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: Defeat of the enemy in battle.

symbols.name: Black trapezoid
symbols.description: A black trapezoid at the hoist, narrowing toward the fly.

facts: The colour meanings come from al-Hilli's poem: 'White are our deeds, black our battles, green our fields, and red our swords.'
The UAE flag uses the same colours with a red band at the hoist instead.
Kuwait's flag is one of the few with a trapezoid.
clues: Green, white and red bands with a black trapezoid at the hoist.
Its colours are described in a medieval line of poetry about deeds, battles, fields and swords.
It replaced a red flag bearing the country's name in 1961.
